summary: An upsert inserts a row, or updates the existing row if one with the same key is already there. Use it to save a value without checking first whether the row exists.
notes: ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE is the syntax in SQLite and PostgreSQL. MySQL uses ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, and SQL Server uses MERGE.
excluded.grade is the value from the row you tried to insert (88 or 92).
The conflict columns must match a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint, here (student_id, course_id, semester).
pitfall: A plain INSERT of an existing key fails with Runtime error: UNIQUE constraint failed: enrollments.student_id, enrollments.course_id, enrollments.semester (19). INSERT OR REPLACE avoids the error but deletes the old row first, so any column you leave out becomes NULL.
